title: Combinators and pseudo-classes
summary: Select elements by where they sit in the page and by their position or state.

options: Only links that are direct children of nav
Every link anywhere inside a nav, at any depth
quiz.explain: A space is the descendant combinator: any `a` inside `nav`, however deep.

options: li elements that are direct children of a ul
Every li inside a ul at any depth
quiz.explain: `>` is the child combinator. It only matches one level down, so it is stricter than a space.

quiz.q: Style a link only while the mouse is over it.
quiz.explain: `:hover` is a pseudo-class for a state. The browser applies it while the pointer is over the element.

quiz.q: A list has items A, B, C, D. Which items does `li:nth-child(2n)` match? Type the letters separated by a space.
quiz.explain: `2n` means the 2nd, 4th, 6th... children, which are B and D. `odd` and `even` are handy shortcuts.

exercise.task:
Style the menu list. Work in `index.html`.

- Make links inside the `nav` have `color: darkgreen` (descendant selector).
- Make only the direct child `li` items of `ul.menu` have `font-weight: bold` using `>`.
- Make the first `li` of `ul.menu` have `color: crimson` using `:first-child`.
- Give every even `li` of `ul.menu` a `background-color` of `lightyellow` using `:nth-child`.
hints: A space between two selectors means descendant. `>` means direct child. Pseudo-classes start with a colon.
Write `nav a`, `ul.menu > li`, `ul.menu > li:first-child` and `ul.menu > li:nth-child(even)`.

checks.name: Links in the nav are dark green
The first menu item is crimson
The second menu item has a light yellow background
The third menu item has no yellow background
checks.hint: Even only: :nth-child(even) skips the odd items.
